0.original: Linuhanu wishes to take you to the shipwright.

29.original: Search Cave Kikitola and obtain raw abokixa.

30.original: Show the raw abokixa to Linuhanu.

31.original: Deliver the raw abokixa to Wuk Evu.

48.original: We're making progress now! The solution to Ok'hanu's woes is as good as found!

49.original: I wonder what manner of shipwright repairs reed-woven boats...

50.original: The shipwright's name is Wuk Evu. He's a Xbr'aal who only moved to Kozama'uka a few years ago, but has since mastered our customs to an almost frightening degree.

51.original: He's especially strict when it comes to manners, so make sure to offer him a proper Hanuhanu greeting. We wouldn't want to offend him right before asking a favor.

52.original: A proper Hanuhanu greeting...? Oh, <hex:021A020203>that<hex:021A020103> one!

53.original: Don't worry, I remember how it goes!

54.original: Then we shouldn't have any problems. Let's head to Ok'bek'be, to the east of here.

55.original: Look over there! Do you see that big, winding staircase!?

56.original: Oh, it seems they have a place here where visitors can stay. Looks cozy.

57.original: This is Ok'bek'be, the Village of All. Those who drift into Kozama'uka from Tuliyollal and elsewhere are welcome to live here alongside the Hanu.

58.original: As for Wuk Evu, he lives and works in the House of Waters High, at the top of that large tree nearby. Follow me, but I should warn you: the climb up the stairs can be challenging.

60.original: I should mention that Wuk Evu isn't only a stickler for etiquette. He is also... Well, you'll find out soon enough.

61.original: We <hex:021A020203>are<hex:021A020103> hoping to enlist the man's aid, so it pays not to be rude in any case.

62.original: A rather eccentric fellow, but I feel his heart is in the right place!

63.original: Cave Kikitola is southwest of Ok'hanu. We can return to the village first, then head there on foot.

64.original: I almost envy how effortlessly he can shift from one mood to its polar opposite. At least I presume he does so by choice...

65.original: Southwest of here, was it? Let us be on our way.

66.original: Look, you can see the falls at the back of the cave! These hollows must have been carved out by the constant deluge of water from above...

67.original: Cave Kikitola, as promised. Home to many deadly creatures. Venture inside if you feel confident, but I will conduct my own search out here.

68.original: You can spot raw abokixa by its green-hued glimmer. Bring anything matching that description to me.

69.original: I shall help scour the inside of the cave, then. You take the west half and I'll take the east!

70.original: I am reluctant to send you into danger for the sake of the float, but if you are willing...

71.original: Upon closer inspection, you find that the glimmer you spied was just light reflecting off the water...

72.original: A shiny pebble catches your eye, but its coloring is grey rather than green.

73.original: You find a chunk of stone glowing a distinct shade of green. This seems like the exact kind of mineral Linuhanu was looking for.

74.original: Some of the cave's inhabitants took umbrage at my presence, but it was nothing a few swishes of my brush couldn't handle.

75.original: I picked over the ground near the entrance but found nothing. Did you have better luck inside the cave?

76.original: Yes, this is abokixa. Along with Krile's contribution, we have more than enough for our needs.

77.original: The stones you've brought shine very brightly. I thank you both.

78.original: ...He would have been happy to know we were putting things right.

79.original: Truth be told, a good friend of mine was meant to be festival leader for this year's Ihih'hana.

80.original: But when that big storm hit, he...he did not survive. It fell to me to carry on in his stead.

81.original: That was why you agreed to Wuk Lamat's request, despite your initial reluctance.

82.original: Yes. It hurt to hear, but she was right. Though I must mourn, I cannot let my grief consume me.

83.original: Her words made me realize that the path to my recovery─our recovery─is already laid out before me. And I will walk it. For myself, and for my friend.

84.original: Thank you for sharing your story with us. Please, rest assured that we've taken your plight to heart.

85.original: I'm certain our companions are procuring the other materials as we speak.

86.original: Everything will come together, and the Hanu shall host a splendid, uplifting festival!

88.original: With that, let us return and deliver the abokixa into Wuk Evu's waiting hands.

89.original: We just got back ourselves. Did you find the stone we needed?

90.original: I hope Wuk Lamat's foray was as productive as ours.

91.original: We've come too far to stop now. The Lifting of Wings must go on!

92.original: Thanks to the Third Promise and her mighty swings, we've collected some suitable logs of uyuipo. What of the abokixa?

93.original: Yes, these are excellent samples. A goodly quantity, too.

94.original: At this stage, you've likely surmised that the Lifting of Wings encourages the crops to grow─but not exactly <hex:021A020203>how<hex:021A020103>, eh?

95.original: Well, you're in for a treat. If all goes to plan, the results should be <hex:021A020203>spectacular<hex:021A020103>.

96.original: Now, to get to work crafting these pieces for the float. I could use an assistant versed in the arcane arts to enhance the uyuipo's conductivity...

98.original: Then I'd be delighted to help.

99.original: Everyone else should head back to Ok'hanu. We'll join you at the float once the work here is complete.

100.original: I'm excited to see how Ihih'hana turns out!

101.original: The final touches are fairly routine and shouldn't take long. Go ahead and wait by the float.

102.original: As Wuk Evu said, the festival really is a spectacle to behold.

103.original: Gathering the uyuipo was a trial in and of itself.

104.original: At first, Wuk Evu criticized everything I did. Then he suddenly yelled “I've spoken ill of the Third Promise and must punish myself!” and proceeded to slam his head into an uyuipo tree...

105.original: I told him not to worry about it─again─and it was like snuffing out a candle. He's an odd one, that's for sure!

106.original: At least we've seen to the poles and the new eye. Now we just have to wait for the feathers from the twins!
